content_units: Board Game Night Shortlist for 6 Adults

These picks all play well in   90 minutes or less  , set up quickly, and avoid heavy war themes. They’re especially good when   one player is newer to modern board games   and the rest may want something still engaging.
Best-Fit Game Comparison
Game   Player Count Fit   Complexity (1-5)   Why It Works for Mixed-Experience Groups
Just One   6/6   1   Cooperative word game with almost no rules overhead; experienced players can help without dominating.
Sushi Go Party!   6/6   1   Fast drafting, cute theme, and simple turns make it easy for new players while still rewarding smart choices.
Wavelength   6/6   1   Team-based guessing sparks conversation and laughter; newcomers can contribute immediately.
Camel Up   6/6   2   Chaotic betting and racing create excitement without punishing inexperience too hard.
Ticket to Ride: Europe   5-6/6   2   Very approachable route-building with clear goals; enough strategy for hobby players without overwhelming a beginner.
For Sale   6/6   2   Short auction game with easy rules, quick rounds, and fun table talk.

Cascadia   4/6 ideal, 6 with rotation if available in your collection only if using expansion; otherwise skip for this group   2   Gentle tile-laying and satisfying choices; great for mixed skill levels, but base game is not a true 6-player fit.
Recommended Picks
Option 1:   Just One     Best opener or closer; cooperative and beginner-safe     Fastest teach
- Great if you want everyone laughing within 5 minutes.
- No player elimination, no complex turns, very low pressure.
Option 2:   Sushi Go Party!     Best all-around light strategy pick for 6     Excellent 6-player fit
- Everyone plays simultaneously, so downtime stays low.
- New players learn by doing after one round.
Option 3:   Wavelength     Best social/team game for mixed personalities     Highly inclusive
- Strong choice if your group likes discussion more than optimization.
- The new player never feels “behind” on rules knowledge.
Option 4:   Camel Up     Best lively competitive game with table energy     Fun chaos
- Easy to explain: watch the race, place bets, enjoy the surprises.
- Experienced gamers can’t perfectly control it, which keeps things even.
Option 5:   Ticket to Ride: Europe     Best classic gateway strategy game     Balanced depth
- Works well if your group wants a “real board game” feel without complexity spikes.
- Slightly longer than the others, but still comfortably under your limit.
Option 6:   For Sale     Best if you want something quick and clever before a bigger game     Very low setup
- Two simple phases and short playtime make it easy to get to the table.
- Good for groups that enjoy light bidding and bluffing.
Option 7:   Dixit Odyssey     Better true 6-player replacement for Cascadia     Creative and accessible
- Beautiful clue-giving and guessing game that welcomes both casual and experienced players.
- Strong fit if your group likes imagination over rules crunch.
Best Hosting Plan for Your Group
For   6 adults with 1 newcomer  , the smoothest lineup is:
-   Start:   Just One or Wavelength
-   Main game:   Sushi Go Party!, Camel Up, or Ticket to Ride: Europe
-   Closer/filler:   For Sale or Dixit Odyssey
Best overall recommendation:
-   Sushi Go Party!   if you want the safest all-around pick
-   Camel Up   if you want the most laughter and table energy
-   Ticket to Ride: Europe   if you want a slightly more strategic centerpiece
Quick Actions
See rules videos
Compare ratings
Game Notes for This Recommendation
I prioritized:
-   Works well at 6
-   Low setup time
-   Playable in 90 minutes or less
-   Welcoming to one newer player
-   Non-war theme
One adjustment:   Cascadia base game is not a standard 6-player recommendation  , so   Dixit Odyssey   is the stronger true fit for your specific group size.
